q: What does HTML stand for?
explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. It is the standard language used to create and structure content on the web.

q: Which tag is used for the largest heading in HTML?
explanation: <h1> is the largest and most important heading tag. Headings go from h1 (biggest) to h6 (smallest). Use only one h1 per page.

q: Which tag is used to create a paragraph in HTML?
explanation: is the paragraph tag. It wraps a block of text and automatically adds spacing above and below the paragraph.

q: Which tag is used to add a line break in HTML?
explanation: is a self-closing tag that forces the content after it onto a new line. It has no closing tag.

q: Which tag makes text bold in HTML?
explanation: <b> makes text visually bold. <strong> also makes text bold but adds extra meaning — it tells search engines the text is important.

q: Which tag is used to insert an image in HTML?
explanation: is used to display images. It requires the src attribute for the image path and the alt attribute for accessibility.

q: Which attribute is used to specify the URL in an anchor tag?
explanation: The href (Hypertext Reference) attribute inside the <a> tag defines the URL the link will go to when clicked.

q: What does target='_blank' do in an anchor tag?

options.A: Opens the link in the same tab
options.C: Opens the link in a new tab

explanation: target='_blank' opens the link in a new browser tab. target='_self' (the default) opens it in the same tab.

q: Which tag draws a horizontal line in HTML?
explanation: <hr> (Horizontal Rule) draws a horizontal line across the page. It is used to visually separate sections of content.

q: Which tag displays text as subscript (below baseline)?
explanation: <sub> displays text below the normal baseline and smaller. Example: H<sub>2</sub>O for water formula.

q: Which tag displays text as superscript (above baseline)?
explanation: <sup> displays text above the normal baseline and smaller. Example: A<sup>2</sup> for math powers.

q: Which tag preserves spaces and line breaks exactly as written?
explanation: <pre> (Preformatted text) displays text exactly as written — preserving all spaces and line breaks. Great for showing code.

q: Which is the correct semantic tag for the main content area of a page?
explanation: <main> represents the primary content of a page. There should be only one <main> tag per page. It tells browsers and search engines where the core content is.

q: Which tag is a block-level container used to group elements?
explanation: <div> is a block-level container. It takes the full width of its parent and starts on a new line. Used to group and organize HTML elements.

q: Which tag is an inline container used to style part of a text?
explanation: <span> is an inline element — it does not break the line and only takes as much width as its content. Used to style a specific word or phrase.

q: Which semantic tag represents the top section of a webpage?
explanation: <header> is a semantic tag for the top section of a page or section. It usually contains the logo, site name, and navigation. Note: <head> is different — it holds metadata.

q: Which semantic tag represents the bottom section of a webpage?
explanation: <footer> is a semantic tag for the bottom section of a page. It usually contains copyright info, contact details, and social links.

q: Which tag is used for table header cells?
explanation: <th> (Table Header) is used for header cells in a table. Text inside <th> is bold and centered by default. <td> is used for regular data cells.

q: What does the colspan attribute do in a table?

options.C: Merges multiple columns into one cell

explanation: colspan='n' makes a table cell span across n columns — similar to merging cells in Excel. Example: colspan='2' makes one cell take the space of two columns.

q: Which tag is used to collect user input in HTML?
explanation: <input> is used inside a <form> to collect data from the user. The type attribute changes its behavior — type='text', type='password', type='email' etc.

q: Write the correct HTML code to create a clickable image that opens https://google.com in a new tab.
What is the difference between <div> and <span>? Give one example of each.
explanation: div is a block element (takes full width). span is an inline element (takes content width only).

q: What does CSS stand for?
explanation: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets. It is used to describe the style of an HTML document.

q: Which of these is NOT a valid way to add CSS to an HTML page?
explanation: A Python script is not a valid method for embedding or linking CSS into an HTML page.

q: Which selector is used to select an element by its class?
explanation: Class selectors in CSS are denoted with a dot (.) prefix.

q: Which selector is used to select an element by its id?
explanation: ID selectors in CSS are denoted with a hash (#) prefix.

q: color: rgb(255, 0, 0); sets the text color to:
explanation: RGB value with full red (255,0,0) targets the red color channel.

q: Which property is used to set the text color of an element?
explanation: The 'color' property sets the text color of an element.

q: Which property sets the background color of an element?
explanation: background-color defines the background area color.

q: font-weight: bold; roughly corresponds to which numeric value?
explanation: Bold text weight generally corresponds to the numeric value 700.

q: Which unit is relative to the font-size of the parent element (for typographic properties)?
explanation: The 'em' unit is relative to the font-size of its direct or inherited parent element.

q: Which unit is always relative to the font-size of the root (html) element?
explanation: 'rem' stands for Root Em, scaling directly with the root HTML tag font size.

q: 96px is roughly equal to how many inches?
explanation: In standard CSS specifications, 96 pixels equals 1 inch.

q: In the CSS box model, which part is the innermost?
explanation: Content sits at the core of the box model, surrounded by padding, border, and margin.

q: Which property is used to round the corners of an element's border?
explanation: border-radius curves the structural corners of a box.

q: An element with display: block; takes up:

options.A: Only the space required by its content

explanation: Block-level elements stretch out horizontally to fill the entire available width.

q: Can margin and padding be applied normally on an element with display: inline;?
explanation: Inline elements do not accept top/bottom margins or vertical padding behavior normally.

q: Which one still reserves the element's space on the page when hidden?
explanation: visibility: hidden hides the visual element but leaves its layout box space intact.

q: Which position value removes an element from the normal flow and positions it relative to its closest positioned ancestor?
explanation: Absolute positioning pulls the element out of flow relative to its nearest positioned ancestor.

q: Which position value keeps an element fixed relative to the browser window, even while scrolling?
explanation: Fixed positioning anchors elements relative to the viewport window.

q: z-index only has an effect when the element's position is:
explanation: z-index applies only to positioned elements (relative, absolute, fixed, sticky).

q: In Flexbox, justify-content controls alignment along the:
explanation: justify-content governs item spacing and distribution along the main flex axis.

q: Complete the CSS rule to set the text color of h1 to red.
explanation: The correct property to style h1 text red is 'color'.

q: Complete the CSS rule to make paragraph text bold.
explanation: font-weight handles bold text formatting.

q: Complete the CSS rule to center-align the text inside a div.
explanation: text-align uses 'center' value for horizontal centering.

q: Complete the CSS rule to set a div height to 50px.
explanation: Height property dictates the vertical dimension size.

q: Complete the CSS rule to make a square div a perfect circle.
explanation: A 50% border radius transforms a square box into a circle.

q: Complete the CSS rule to add inner spacing of 10px inside a div.
explanation: Padding establishes inner spacing around content inside borders.

q: Complete the CSS rule to set outer margin offsets around a div.
explanation: Margin sets outer offsets around box elements.

q: Complete the ID selector rule to style an element with id='box'.
explanation: #box targets elements matching ID attribute values.

q: Complete the class selector rule to style elements with class='heading'.
explanation: .heading targets elements sharing the class name.

q: Complete the universal selector rule to reset margin and padding on all elements.
explanation: The asterisk (*) selects all elements in the document.

q: Complete the CSS rule to underline anchor tag links.
explanation: text-decoration handles underlines and line styling.

q: Complete the CSS rule to transform paragraph text to uppercase.
explanation: text-transform controls letter capitalization formatting.

q: Complete the CSS rule to completely hide and remove a div from the document layout.
explanation: display: none completely deletes element rendering and flow footprint.

q: Complete the CSS rule to lock a div position relative to the browser viewport.
explanation: fixed positioning locks elements relative to screen scroll behavior.

q: Definition Task: Define CSS in your own words. What kind of language is it, and why do we need it alongside HTML?
explanation: CSS is a style sheet language used for describing the presentation of a document written in HTML. We need it to separate structure from design/layout.

q: Definition Task: What is a 'selector' in CSS? Give one example of a class selector and one example of an id selector.
explanation: Selectors are patterns used to select the element(s) you want to style. Example class selector: .card; Example id selector: #header.

q: Definition Task: What is the CSS Box Model? Name its four parts, from innermost to outermost.
explanation: The box model is a box that wraps around every HTML element. Four parts from inside out: Content, Padding, Border, Margin.

q: Definition Task: What is the difference between display: none; and visibility: hidden;?
explanation: display: none removes the element entirely from the layout, while visibility: hidden hides it visually but keeps its spatial footprint intact.

q: Definition Task: What is Flexbox used for? Explain the difference between the 'main axis' and the 'cross axis'.
explanation: Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout model for aligning items. The main axis is the primary direction along which flex items are laid out, and the cross axis runs perpendicular to it.

q: Coding Task 1: Style a Button — Create a button and set its background color to green using internal or inline styling rules.
explanation:
<button class="btn">Click Me</button>
.btn { background-color: green; padding: 10px 20px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 14px; }

q: Coding Task 2: Simple Navbar — Style the navbar so three links sit next to each other in a single line evenly spaced using display: flex.
explanation:
nav { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; }
nav a { text-decoration: none; color: #222; }

q: Coding Task 3: Simple Profile Card — Give the profile card a border, padding, and fixed width.
explanation: .profile-card { border: 1px solid #ccc; padding: 16px; width: 300px; }

q: Coding Task 4: Center 3 Boxes — Center 3 small boxes both vertically and horizontally inside a big parent box using Flexbox.
explanation:
.parent { height: 220px; border: 1px solid #ccc; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; }
.box { width: 50px; height: 50px; background: teal; color: white; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; margin: 0 6px; }

q: Coding Task 5: Perfect Circle — Turn a 100px x 100px box into a perfect circle with background color using border-radius.
explanation: .circle { width: 100px; height: 100px; background-color: #f5a623; border-radius: 50%; }

q: Which CSS property specifies the stack order of positioned elements?
explanation: z-index manages overlapping element stacking tiers.

q: How do you specify multiple fallback font families in CSS?
explanation: font-family values use comma separation to designate fallback hierarchy.

q: Which property controls the space between individual characters in a word?
explanation: letter-spacing adjusts gaps between letters.

q: Which property sets the transparency or opacity of an entire element container?
explanation: opacity governs transparent rendering levels from 0 to 1.

q: What is the default value of flex-direction in a flex container?
explanation: Flexbox containers align children horizontally by default via 'row'.

q: Which CSS property sets spacing between rows and columns inside a grid or flex layout?
explanation: The 'gap' property manages gutters between layout cells or items efficiently.
